{"files": [{"content": "# Blackout

Blackout lets you think out loud without looking at a screen while an AI quietly keeps track, then turns what you said into a cited summary, a clean mind map, and a one-page hand-drawn picture.

## Problem

People who stare at screens all day struggle to do thinking work (planning, brainstorming, clarifying ideas) without getting distracted. The tool they work with and the thing that distracts them are the same screen.

Most focus apps try to remind you to concentrate. Blackout takes a different approach: let people get the thinking done without looking at the screen at all.

## What it is

Blackout is a thinking tool, not a health or attention treatment. The concept is 关灯 → 星图 → 开灯 (lights off → star map → lights on):

- You press **关灯 / Lights off**. The screen goes pure black (#000). You think out loud — walking around, lying down, or sketching on paper — with no keys to press.
- A separate **star map window （星图）**, opened for video viewers on a second screen or in a second window, shows the thought process appearing live as a real mind map: points, decisions, todos, questions, and contradictions as glowing nodes around your goal.
- When you say 「结束」or "Stop.", **the light comes on at once**: the black page fades to paper and the result page appears immediately. Its content then fills in as it becomes ready, so you are never left staring at a black or blank screen while整理 is still running.
- A final pass then reads everything you said and produces a short summary, a clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions. Every item cites the sentences （原话） it came from, and an item with no valid citation is dropped by the server rather than shown. A later statement replaces an earlier one, so changing your mind is recorded as a change, not reported as a contradiction.
- `muse-image-1.0` then draws a one-page hand-drawn summary picture from that checked summary — with timelines, flows, and lists where they fit, and the exact text from the summary. Its web search is turned off, and one picture costs $0.01. The picture can be downloaded or redrawn. The explanation picture on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.
- Because you may not be looking yet when the session ends, the summary is also read aloud. You hear the outcome first; the page, the clean map, and the picture are there when you do look.

The AI listens continuously and stays silent by default. It tracks the line of thought against your goal and speaks only when useful. When the session ends, you have a short summary, a clean mind map, decisions, todos, a parking lot for off-topic ideas, unresolved questions, contradictions that were not simply later changes of mind, unfinished points, anything you asked it to look up or draft, and the hand-drawn picture.

## No accounts: a browser owns its sessions

Every visitor starts with a brand-new app. There are no accounts, no usernames, and no passwords: a browser is the unit of ownership, through an HttpOnly cookie, and the server stores only its hash. The raw cookie value is not stored in the session records. People cannot list, read, change, delete, or spend through anyone else's sessions — session lists, session records, turns, background work, sketches, results, pictures, announcements, live state, and deletion are all scoped to the owning browser. Your own past sessions are behind one quiet link on the start page, not shown as a public list to other visitors.

## English and Chinese

Blackout works in English and Chinese. The UI follows the browser language and can be switched on the page. The AI replies, the summary, and the picture follow the language spoken in the session, and end phrases work in both languages — for example 「结束」in Chinese and "Stop." in English. You do not need to set the spoken language separately from how you actually speak.

## How it differs from a voice assistant

A normal voice assistant is question-and-answer: you ask, it answers every time. Blackout manages attention:

- Silence is the main behaviour. Most turns get no reply at all, just a very quiet tick so you know you were heard.
- It tracks the line of thought against a stated goal. It notices unfinished points and contradictions and asks short follow-ups at natural pauses.
- When you drift off-topic, it stores the idea in a parking lot and pulls you back, instead of chatting along.
- Speaking is deliberately rationed: a minimum gap between spoken interventions, with pull-backs and direct answers exempt.
- It ends with one structured page: a cited summary, goal, clean mind map, decisions, todos, parking lot, unresolved questions, contradictions, unfinished points, background results, and the hand-drawn picture.

The black screen shows nothing to read. All AI replies are voice-only, so eyes stay off the screen.

## A short demo of the flow

1. On the start page you say or type a goal, for example “想清楚比赛 demo 的技术方案” or "Figure out how to take my parents to Suzhou for one day this Saturday", and press 关灯 / Lights off. If you are recording video, you tick 录视频：同时打开星图窗口 / Record video: also open the star map window first — fullscreen is skipped in that mode, by design, so both windows stay reachable. The start page also shows an explanation picture drawn by Muse Image, so you can see what the end of a session produces.
2. The screen goes pure black (#000) with only a dim corner dot (paused / listening / AI speaking / reconnecting). A spoken line tells you the controls, because you are no longer looking.
3. You think out loud, hands-free — no keys needed. The AI stays quiet while the star map window quietly fills in the mind map.
4. You drift: “对了，中午吃火锅吧。” or "By the way, I want hot pot tonight." The AI parks it and brings you back in one sentence.
5. You ask: “帮我查一下……” or "Please look up …" It works in the background while you keep talking, then reports back in one spoken sentence. Nothing appears on the black screen.
6. You go quiet over an unfinished point; after a silence it nudges once, naming that point.
7. You say “结束” or "Stop." (or press Esc). It says it will整理 / put it together, the light comes on at once, and the result page appears immediately while the final pass runs. When it is ready, the summary is read aloud, and the page fills in with the short summary, the clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, unresolved questions, the other recorded sections, and — drawn by `muse-image-1.0` for $0.01 — the one-page hand-drawn picture with its timelines, flows, and lists. You can download the picture or ask for it to be redrawn. Every summary item can be expanded to show the exact sentences it came from.

## How to stop, and other audible controls

You never need to look at the screen to stop. An utterance ends the session when its *last clause* is an end phrase — in Chinese: “结束”, “结束吧”, “结束了”, “停止”, “停”, “我说完了”, “说完了”, “就到这”, “就到这里”, “到这吧”, “不说了”, “先这样”; in English, end phrases including "Stop." work the same way — so “好，结束。” works, and “首先我觉得有个问题，好，结束” first records the thought, then ends. You can also press Esc, leave fullscreen, or (on a phone) hold a touch for 800 ms. If the browser leaves fullscreen with Esc, the session ends the same way, so you are never stuck on a black screen.

Every state and instruction is audible because the product is used without looking:

- On entering the black screen the app speaks, in the language in use, the equivalent of: “黑屏开始。我在听，你直接说就行。按空格暂停，想结束就说结束，或者按 Esc。”
- In hands-free mode, Space or a short tap pauses and resumes, with rising/falling cues. Holding Space does not toggle repeatedly.
- The microphone stays on while the AI speaks, so you can talk over it: a real interruption cuts the AI off immediately and it stops. Muting during playback would lose whatever you said at that moment, which breaks the core promise that everything said is kept. Echo of the AI's own voice is separated from real speech on the server by comparing the recognised text with what was just spoken.
- A soft tick confirms you were heard, a two-note chime precedes background announcements, and rising/falling cues mark push-to-talk recording in fallback mode.
- If hands-free streaming is unavailable, the app says so and switches to push-to-talk: Space or tap starts and stops recording, recordings are uploaded as WAV, and announcements are polled and spoken.
- On ending, the final summary is read aloud once it is ready, because you may still not be looking at the screen.

## The star map window （星图）

Ticking “录视频：同时打开星图窗口” / "Record video: also open the star map window" on the start page (or opening `/observer?session=<id>` on a second screen) shows a large-type, high-contrast, dark view designed to read clearly in a 1280×720 video without scrolling. It is built for video viewers: the goal as the central star, a microphone state indicator （在听 / 暂停 / 你在说 / AI 在说 / 未连接， or the English equivalents), the live caption, the last AI decision and why, and the mind map growing in real time — main points marked 已展开/未展开, with decisions, todos, questions, and contradictions nested under the points they belong to. The parking lot sits at the side (briefly highlighted when something new is parked), and counters show how much you have said versus how often the AI has spoken and pulled you back. When the session finishes, the live map tidies into the clean mind map from the final pass, and the window shows the result title and stops polling. The star map never shows money, and it never appears in the black-screen flow.

## A real mind map, not a flat list

The tree is built by the server, deterministically, from what was recorded. Each turn, the model returns *additions only* — never a rewritten state, so nothing you said can be lost — and each addition carries an `under` field naming the existing point it belongs to. The server places:

- sub-points under their parent point,
- decisions, todos, questions, and contradictions under the point they belong to (or directly under the goal when they have no parent),
- background tasks under their point, showing the instruction while running and the conclusion when done.

That same tree renders as the animated star map in the star map window, as the static map at the top of the result page, and as a nested outline in the copied Markdown. At the end of a session the final pass reads every utterance again and tidies this into the clean mind map used on the result page; the live, additive record underneath is not rewritten or lost.

## The final pass: summary, citations, and picture

When a session ends, one final pass reads every utterance from the session — not just the running notes — and produces:

- a short summary,
- a clean mind map,
- complete decisions and todos,
- unresolved questions.

Every item in that output must cite the sentences it came from. The server checks each citation against the actual utterances: an item whose citations are missing or do not match anything that was said is dropped, not displayed. A later statement replaces an earlier one on the same point, so a change of mind is shown as the current position and is not reported as a contradiction. Contradictions are reserved for conflicts that were never resolved by a later statement.

From that checked summary, `muse-image-1.0` draws a one-page hand-drawn summary picture: timelines, flows, and lists are used where they fit what was said, and the text in the picture is the exact text from the summary. The image call has web search turned off, and costs $0.01 per picture. On the result page the picture can be downloaded, or redrawn if a new drawing is wanted. The explanation picture shown on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.

The page lights up at once when the session ends, and each part — summary, clean map, lists, picture — fills in when it is ready. The summary is read aloud when it arrives, because the person using Blackout may not be looking at the screen yet.

## Architecture

- Backend: Python FastAPI in `app/`, thread-based; blocking model calls run in threads, and the WebSocket bridge uses asyncio with `asyncio.to_thread`.
  - `app/main.py`: app creation, middleware, error envelope, static files, router wiring.
  - `app/routes.py`: HTTP routes.
  - `app/security.py`: host and origin checks, access token, rate limit, security headers, body-size limits, and browser-ownership checks.
  - `app/realtime.py`: WebSocket bridge between the browser and the realtime speech API, including echo/interruption handling, coalescing of turns, delivery that never talks over the user, silence nudges, reconnects, and audio accounting.
  - `app/asr.py`: upstream realtime speech connection, handshake, and real-time pacing with a silence pump.
  - `app/conductor.py`: one turn of the conversation; decides what the AI does.
  - `app/state.py` / `app/store.py`: pure thinking-state functions (including the mind-map tree builder) and per-session persistence with locks.
  - `app/tasks.py`: background search and drafting on a thread pool.
  - `app/summary.py`: the final pass and result page content — cited summary, clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions, degrading to the stored lists if the model call fails.
  - `app/sketch.py`: paper-sketch understanding from a photo uploaded on the result page.
  - `app/prompts.py`: every prompt and JSON schema.
  - `app/phone.py`: LAN HTTPS launcher for phones (see below).
  - `app/static/`: `index.html`, `observer.html`, `app.css`, `observer.css`, `map.css`, and `js/*.js` — no framework, no external resources, no inline script or style; everything rendered from the server or the model uses `textContent`.
- Voice in (hands-free): `getUserMedia` + `AudioContext` + `AudioWorklet` captures 24 kHz mono PCM in 80 ms frames streamed over a WebSocket. While paused, zeroed frames are sent instead; while the AI speaks, the microphone keeps capturing (see above).
- Voice out: browser `speechSynthesis`, preferring a natural/online voice in the language in use (for example `zh-CN` for Chinese), then a matching-language voice. There is no text-to-speech model in this project; speech output is the browser's.
- State is saved after every turn to one JSON file per session, written atomically, so a refresh, crash, or restart loses nothing. A task still marked `running` when a session is loaded after a restart becomes `failed`.
- Ownership: there are no accounts. Each browser receives an HttpOnly ownership cookie; only a hash of that value is stored on the server, and every session access is checked against the owning browser.
- Language: the UI follows the browser language and can be switched on the page; the AI replies, the summary, and the picture follow the language spoken, and end phrases work in English and Chinese.

## How it uses Meta models

All model access goes through the preconfigured Muse client (`muse_client.py`, key read from `MODEL_API_KEY`); the key never reaches the browser or the logs, and speech and transcripts are never logged.

- `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` — speech recognition. In hands-free mode it is used over the realtime WebSocket (`wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime`) in endpointing mode with cumulative partials, so the app hears continuous speech, natural pauses, and interruptions. For push-to-talk and goal dictation, the same model transcribes uploaded WAV via `POST /asr/transcribe`.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — the conductor. Each turn sends the goal, the current thinking state, the last 12 history messages, and the new utterance, and returns strict structured additions (never a rewritten state, so nothing you said can be lost) plus one of: listen, follow up, pull back, continue, answer, summarise, or start a background task. Each addition names the point it belongs under.
- `muse-spark-1.3` with the built-in `web_search` tool — background search for “帮我查一下……” / "Please look up …". The first sentence of the result is a short spoken conclusion, the rest and the sources are stored for the result page.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — background drafting for “帮我写一段……” / a drafting request. Drafts are never read aloud; they appear on the result page.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — sketch understanding. A photo of a paper sketch is sent with the goal and state; only what is visibly on the paper is recorded.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — the final pass. When a session ends it reads every utterance and returns a short summary, a clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions, each item citing the sentences it came from. The server validates those citations and drops any item without a valid one; a later statement replaces an earlier one, so a change of mind is not reported as a contradiction. If the model call fails for any reason, the result page degrades to the stored lists instead of failing.
- `muse-image-1.0` — the one-page hand-drawn summary picture drawn from the final summary, using timelines, flows, and lists where they fit, with the exact text from the summary and its web search turned off. One picture costs $0.01. The picture can be downloaded or redrawn from the result page, and the explanation picture on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.
- Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`) and Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) — the coding models that generated the code in this repository (see “How this project was built”). Of the two, only `muse-spark-1.3` is also used by the running product; `muse-wonder-1.0` is not.

Background work is deliberately bounded: each session may start at most 12 background tasks in total, and a task whose instruction duplicates one already started in the same session (ignoring punctuation and spaces) is refused — the question is kept as an open question instead of being searched or written twice.

## How to run on a computer

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Create a `.env` file in the repo root (this file is not committed) and write your key:

```
MODEL_API_KEY=your-key-here
```

Then start the server from the repo root:

```bash
python -m uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. Type or speak a goal, press 关灯 / Lights off, think out loud hands-free, say “结束” or "Stop." or press Esc to finish. To see your own earlier sessions, use the one quiet link to past sessions on the start page; a different browser will start empty.

Run tests:

```bash
pytest
```

## How to run on a phone

Phones only allow the microphone over HTTPS, so use the phone launcher from the repo root:

```bash
python -m app.phone
```

It detects your LAN IP, generates (or reuses, while the IP still matches) a self-signed certificate in the `tls` folder inside the data location described under Privacy below, creates a random access token, and starts the server on `https://<your-lan-ip>:8443`. It prints the full URL — including the token — and a terminal QR code (if the optional `segno` package is installed; otherwise it prints the URL only). Scan it or type the URL on the phone. The phone will warn about the self-signed certificate once; accept it, and the token is stored in a secure cookie so the warning URL is not needed again. Keep the phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi network. The default computer mode above stays bound to 127.0.0.1 with no token; the access token, host/origin checks, and rate limit in `app/security.py` protect the phone mode, because this server can spend your money.

## Spend control

`budget.py` is the only hard spending limit and is enforced locally before any paid call: a JSONL ledger records actual token, search, audio, and image costs, and calls are refused with HTTP 402 once the cap (`STOP_AT_USD`, $140) would be exceeded. The ledger lives in the data location described under Privacy — `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blackout` on Windows, `~/.blackout` elsewhere — regardless of `BLACKOUT_DATA_DIR`, so a temporary data directory can never reset the total; `BLACKOUT_LEDGER_FILE` overrides the ledger path explicitly. Realtime audio is metered by the second of audio actually forwarded. Each hand-drawn summary picture from `muse-image-1.0` costs $0.01 and is recorded the same way. `GET /api/status` reports `spent_usd` and `limit_usd` for the local operator; the star map window never shows money. Budget exhaustion is announced by voice and ends hands-free sessions cleanly; summaries degrade to the stored lists instead of failing.

## Privacy

Everything Blackout stores lives on your own machine in one place: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blackout` on Windows and `~/.blackout` elsewhere (sessions can be redirected with `BLACKOUT_DATA_DIR`). That one location holds the session files (one JSON per session), the spend ledger, and the phone-mode TLS files; the spend ledger stays there regardless of `BLACKOUT_DATA_DIR`, and `BLACKOUT_LEDGER_FILE` overrides the ledger path. Nothing is sent anywhere except the Meta Model API: your goal, conversation text, and (for searches) the search instruction go to `muse-spark-1.3`, your audio goes to `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0`, and the checked final summary goes to `muse-image-1.0` to be drawn. Speech and transcripts are never written to server logs, and the API key never reaches the browser or the logs. Web content returned by background search is treated as untrusted data: it is stored and spoken, never allowed to change state or trigger actions. The image call has web search turned off.

Browser ownership is not an account: the browser holds an HttpOnly cookie, the server stores only its hash, and that hash is what scopes access to that browser's sessions. No list of users is kept.

## Limitations, stated honestly

- **This is built to run on your own computer or LAN. A public deployment would also need per-visitor spending limits, an access code, and data expiry, which are not built yet.**
- **Clearing the browser's cookies loses access to past sessions.** Because a browser is the unit of ownership and there are no accounts, there is no sign-in or recovery flow to get that access back.
- Speech output quality depends entirely on the device and browser: it uses the browser's `speechSynthesis`, and speech output is not a Meta model. Without a suitable English or Chinese voice installed, the AI may be hard to understand; Chrome or Edge with a `zh-CN` voice works best for Chinese.
- Speech recognition is tuned for Mandarin Chinese and English; heavy dialect, noise, or crosstalk will produce mistakes, and echo detection — though text-based — is not perfect on speakers with strong reverberation.
- The final summary is only as good as what was recognised and said. Citations are checked against the recorded utterances and uncited items are dropped, but a mis-recognised sentence can still be cited faithfully.
- The hand-drawn picture is generated from the checked summary text, and the call is made with web search turned off; like any generated picture, a redraw may be needed if a drawing comes out unclear, which is why the result page offers one.
- The phone flow has a one-time self-signed certificate warning, and requires the phone and computer to share a LAN.
- Testing so far, stated plainly: automated end-to-end runs used a simulated microphone with English speech and a simulated speech output; Chinese speech was tried by the author on a real computer; the phone flow has been exercised over HTTPS in a desktop browser, not yet on a physical phone. There is no usage data yet: Blackout has not been tested with anyone beyond its author, and no effectiveness claims are made. It is a thinking tool, not a treatment for attention problems, and it gives no health advice.
- A session is designed for up to about an hour of continuous hands-free audio; the bridge reconnects transparently across the speech API's 60-minute connection limit, but very long sessions are untested.

## How this project was built

Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, through the Meta Model API, generated the code in this repository, including the app, infrastructure, tests, and docs. Raw model output is in `muse_runs/`.

The author provided the idea and tried the product.

Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent) drafted the prompts in `spec/` from the author's idea, ran the generation, reviewed and tested the output, and made the git commits.

A separate security review by Claude Code produced findings that Muse then fixed.

Defects found in review and in the author's own use were written up in `spec/feedback_*.md`, and Muse generated every fix.

The staged v2 build-out, including this star map window, phone mode, the final cited summary, the hand-drawn picture, and documentation stage, was specified in the `spec/stage_*.md` files alongside the earlier `spec/feedback_*.md` notes; each stage was generated by Muse from its stage file, reviewed, and tested the same way.

Generation was not run as one whole-project prompt: a prompt covering the whole project at once made the model unreliable, producing inconsistent and incomplete output. Instead, `build_with_muse.py` is invoked per stage with `--context` to supply the relevant existing files and `--expect` to declare the files that stage must return, so each generation is scoped to the stage's spec and its output can be checked against the expected file list before anything is accepted.

The first two commits contain earlier infrastructure files written by Claude Code. Muse regenerated them later from a behaviour description in `spec/feedback_05.md`, without being shown the earlier source.

## License

MIT — see `LICENSE`.

## One-line concept

Lights off → star map → lights on: the speaker presses Lights off, the screen goes pure black, and the speaker thinks out loud using voice alone; in the star map window, thoughts grow as a mind map; the speaker says "Stop.", the light comes on at once, the summary is read aloud, the star map tidies into a clean map, and a hand-drawn picture fills the screen as the final frame.

## How to record (state this first)

- **Two-window recording**: the black-screen device (phone or computer) stays pure black and is out of shot, or gets only an opening close-up; the recording captures only the **star map window** at 1280×720.
- **What the audience sees**: the star map window. The star map shows the goal, microphone state, live caption, the last AI decision and the reason for that decision, the mind map (points, decisions, todos, questions, and contradictions nested under the point each item belongs to), the parking lot, background tasks, and counters. The star map never shows money.
- **What the audience hears**: the real conversation — the speaker thinking out loud at a black screen, and the AI replying by voice only. Record system sound and microphone on separate tracks.
- **Open on the black screen**: pure black is the most memorable shot. Let the audience see that the screen really is gone, then cut to the star map.
- **End on the hand-drawn picture**: after "Stop." the page lights up at once, the summary is read aloud when ready, the star map tidies into the clean map, one citation is opened on the result page, and the recording ends on the `muse-image-1.0` hand-drawn summary picture full-screen as the final frame.
- **Be honest about the wait**: the final summary takes about **15 to 20 seconds** to generate. Record the full wait once, shorten the wait in editing, and state the edit plainly in a caption or in narration: "The summary takes about 15–20 seconds to generate; that wait has been shortened here." Do not present the summary as instant.
- **Language setting**: set the browser or page language to English before recording, so the UI, the AI replies, the summary, and the picture follow the English spoken in the recording.

---

## Setup checklist

- [ ] On the start page, tick "Record video: also open the star map window". This mode **skips fullscreen by design**, so both windows stay reachable side by side for recording.
- [ ] Computer and phone (if phone mode is used) are on the same Wi-Fi; for phone mode, run `python -m app.phone` first, scan the code, open the URL, and accept the one-time certificate prompt.
- [ ] The browser has an English voice for speech output (and a `zh-CN` voice only if a Chinese take is also planned); the start page shows no warning about a missing voice. Switch the page language to English.
- [ ] The explanation picture drawn by Muse Image is visible and loading normally on the start page.
- [ ] Black-screen device: microphone permission granted, system notifications and pop-ups other than Do Not Disturb prompts turned off, earphones in, or speaker output positioned so the recording captures the AI voice clearly.
- [ ] Goal prepared in advance, typed exactly as: `Figure out how to take my parents to Suzhou for one day this Saturday`
- [ ] Star map open, showing the goal and "Listening".
- [ ] Recording software captures only the star map window (1280×720), with system sound and microphone on separate tracks.
- [ ] Timing rehearsed once in full: the first silence nudge defaults to 60 seconds of silence, so the "unfinished point" beat needs a real wait (the wait may be sped up in editing, but the reason the AI speaks must not be cut).
- [ ] Ending rehearsed once in full: summary read-aloud, opening a citation, and the hand-drawn picture full-screen all work; the real summary wait is about 15–20 seconds and is handled as described above.
- [ ] Network stable; paper and pen within reach (optional, to show drawing without looking at a screen).
- [ ] A fresh browser profile or a new browser gives a brand-new, empty app; use the browser that owns the rehearsal sessions only if past sessions behind the quiet link will not distract from the take.

---

## Shot overview

| Time | Scene | Audience sees (star map / result page) | Audience hears (real conversation) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:20 | Problem + black-screen opening | Star map idle, then the goal appears | Narration + black-screen close-up |
| 0:20–0:35 | Press Lights off, entry line | Goal appears, state "Listening" | Entry line |
| 0:35–1:20 | Thinking out loud, AI stays silent | Mind map grows point by point | The speaker talks continuously; the AI gives only an occasional quiet tick |
| 1:20–1:45 | Drift to hot pot, pulled back | Parking lot briefly highlights a new item | One pull-back sentence |
| 1:45–2:15 | "Please look up …" | Background task "running → done"; the map keeps growing | Confirmation, continued speech, then a one-sentence answer |
| 2:15–2:30 | Unfinished point is named | AI decision becomes a follow-up | A nudge after silence |
| 2:30–3:00 | "Stop.", lights on, clean map, citation, hand-drawn picture | Page lights up at once; star map tidies into the clean map; result page opens one citation; hand-drawn picture full-screen as the final frame | Closing line from the AI, summary read aloud, closing narration (wait shortened, stated honestly) |

---

## 0:00–0:20 Problem + black-screen opening (20 seconds)

**Picture:** Open with a 3-second close-up of the black-screen device — pure black, one dim corner dot only. Hold that shot. Then cut to the idle star map window.

**Narration (record exactly):**

> "To think one thing through, I open a document — and ten minutes later I have checked messages instead. The tool for the work and the thing that distracts me are the same screen. Blackout does not remind me to focus. Blackout removes the screen."

---

## 0:20–0:35 Press Lights off (15 seconds)

**Action:** On the start page, enter the goal `Figure out how to take my parents to Suzhou for one day this Saturday`, with "Record video: also open the star map window" already ticked, and click "Lights off".

**Audience hears (the real entry line from the black-screen device, word for word as spoken by the app; the English equivalent is):**

## If something goes wrong during recording

- **The AI does not pull back after the hot-pot line**: the line was probably too short in context or merged into the previous stretch of speech. Pause for two seconds and repeat, standalone and exactly: "By the way, I want hot pot tonight."
- **The search result is slow to return**: keep going with the food lines; do not wait in silence. A task can complete as late as the result page, and a result page with a running task refreshes on its own.
- **The nudge does not arrive**: check that room noise is not being treated as speech; stay quiet for a full 60 seconds. Only two nudges are given (one after 60 seconds, one after a further 120 seconds); plan the take around that limit.
- **The black-screen device cannot hear clearly**: move closer to the microphone, or press Escape, finish, and re-record the segment; if fallback mode is active, Space starts and stops a recording and the recording is uploaded after the second press.

- **The summary takes much longer than expected**: do not restart the take at once. After the light comes on, content fills in when ready, and a normal wait is about 15 to 20 seconds. - **Text or drawing in the hand-drawn picture is unclear**: click "Redraw" on the result page for another picture (each picture costs $0.01), or click "Download" to save the current picture; end the recording on a clear version, full-screen.
- **An end phrase ends the session early by accident**: treat the result page as the final画面 for that take; to re-record, use "Start again" back to the start page. The earlier session remains in the owner's own past-sessions list in the same browser and can be deleted there.

---

## If recording in Chinese: add English subtitles

A Chinese recording is welcome, with the same structure and the same beats. Record the Chinese take following the sections above, using the Chinese equivalents of the prepared lines — a realistic everyday goal, the hot-pot drift line, a "帮我查一下……" search line, and 「结束」to end — and add English subtitles throughout, because judges may not read Chinese. Keep subtitles faithful to the spoken words rather than summarising the spoken words away, open on the black screen, and end on the hand-drawn picture full-screen, exactly as in the English recording.

## Theme and track

- Theme: Build for Your World
- Track: Indie developer (solo-built)

## One-liner

Blackout lets screen-tired thinkers do planning and brainstorming without looking at the screen — you press 关灯 / Lights off, the screen goes black, a star map window shows your thoughts growing as a real mind map, and when you say “结束” or "Stop." the light comes on at once, the summary is read aloud, and the page fills in with a cited summary, a clean mind map, and a one-page hand-drawn picture.

## The problem in my world

The tool you work with and the thing that distracts you are the same screen. I do my best thinking away from the screen, but all my tools live inside it. Existing focus tools remind you to concentrate; none of them remove the screen itself. I wanted a way to think a plan through eyes-free and still walk away with something written down — and, at the end, something I can trust and something I can see at a glance.

## What it does

The concept is 关灯 → 星图 → 开灯 (lights off → star map → lights on):

1. You type or speak a goal on the start page and press 关灯 ("lights off"). The screen goes pure black (#000) with only a dim corner dot for status; a spoken line explains the controls, because you will not look again. No keys are needed from here on. The start page also shows an explanation picture drawn by Muse Image, so the end product of a session is visible before you start.
2. You think out loud, hands-free. The AI listens continuously and stays silent by default — a soft tick is all you hear for most turns. It tracks your main points against the goal, and speaks only when a point was left unfinished, you contradicted yourself, you drifted off the goal, you asked it something, or you have gone silent.
3. Drift is parked, not followed: the idea goes into a parking lot and one sentence pulls you back. Drift never becomes a conversation.
4. “帮我查一下……” (look this up) / "Please look up …" or “帮我写一段……” (write this) starts background work while you keep talking; a search reports back in one spoken sentence, a draft waits silently for the result page. Background work is capped at 12 tasks per session, and duplicate instructions are refused.
5. The microphone stays on while the AI speaks, so you can talk over it and it stops mid-sentence; its own echo is recognised and discarded on the server by comparing the recognised text against what it just said. If hands-free streaming fails, it says so and falls back to push-to-talk recording.
6. Say “结束” or "Stop." — an utterance ends the session when its last clause is an end phrase, so “好，结束。” works in Chinese and "Stop." works in English — or press Esc, leave fullscreen, or hold a touch on a phone. The page lights up at once: the screen fades from black to paper and the result page appears immediately, with each part filling in when it is ready rather than after everything has finished.
7. A final pass then reads everything you said and produces a short summary, a clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions. Every item cites the sentences it came from, and any item with no valid citation is dropped by the server before it can be shown. A later statement replaces an earlier one, so a change of mind is recorded as the current position and is not reported as a contradiction. Because you may not be looking yet, the summary is read aloud as soon as it is ready.
8. From that checked summary, `muse-image-1.0` draws a one-page hand-drawn summary picture — timelines, flows, and lists where they fit what was said, carrying the exact text from the summary. The image call runs with its web search turned off and costs $0.01 per picture. The picture can be downloaded or redrawn from the result page.
9. The finished page holds the read-aloud summary, the clean mind map, decisions, todos, parking lot, unresolved questions, contradictions, unfinished points, background results with sources, and anything recognised from a photo of your paper sketch — plus a Copy as Markdown button, and the hand-drawn picture.
10. An optional star map window （星图， opened from the start page for a second screen or for video) shows the goal, microphone state, live caption, the AI's last decision and reasoning, the parking lot, and the growing mind map — everything the black screen deliberately hides. When the session ends, that live map tidies into the clean mind map from the final pass. It never shows money.

Unlike a general voice assistant that answers every sentence, Blackout owns the attention: its main behaviour is knowing when to say nothing, it remembers what you left unfinished, refuses to follow distractions, and delivers a page you can act on — one whose every claim can be traced back to something you actually said.

## No accounts, and two languages

Every visitor starts with a brand-new app. There are no accounts: a browser is the unit of ownership, through an HttpOnly cookie, and the server stores only its hash. People cannot list, read, change, delete, or spend through anyone else's sessions. Your own past sessions are behind one quiet link. Blackout is also bilingual: the UI follows the browser and can be switched on the page, the AI replies, the summary, and the picture follow the language spoken, and end phrases work in both English and Chinese. The explanation picture on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.

Blackout is built to run on your own computer or LAN. A public deployment would also need per-visitor spending limits, an access code, and data expiry, which are not built yet. Clearing the browser's cookies loses access to past sessions, because there is no account to sign back into.

## A cited summary, not just a summary

The final pass is deliberately strict about evidence. It reads every utterance from the session and returns a short summary, a clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions. Each item must cite the sentences it came from. The server then checks those citations against the recorded utterances: if an item has no citation, or its citations do not match anything that was actually said, the server drops the item instead of displaying it. On the result page, each item can be expanded to show the exact sentences behind it.

Superseded statements are handled the same way throughout: when a later statement replaces an earlier one on the same point, the later statement is what the summary reports, and the pair is not reported as a contradiction. Contradictions are only the conflicts that were never resolved by a later statement. If the final model call fails for any reason, the page degrades to the lists recorded during the session, with a notice, rather than failing.

## One hand-drawn page

Once the summary has passed the citation check, `muse-image-1.0` draws it as a single hand-drawn page: timelines for sequences, flows for processes, and lists for decisions and todos, using the exact text from the summary rather than paraphrasing it into the image. The image generation runs with web search turned off, so the picture contains only what came from the session, and each picture costs $0.01. On the result page the picture can be downloaded as an image or redrawn. The explanation picture on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.

## A real mind map, not a flat list

Each turn, the model returns additions only — never a rewritten state, so nothing recorded can be lost — and every addition (point, decision, todo, question, contradiction, background task) carries an `under` field naming the existing point it belongs to, or the goal itself. The server builds the tree deterministically from those additions. That tree is rendered as the animated star map in the star map window during the session; at the end, the final pass tidies it into the clean mind map shown on the result page and reflected in the nested outline inside the copied Markdown.

## How it works

- FastAPI backend (Python, thread-based) with a vanilla HTML/CSS/JS frontend. No framework, no external assets, no inline script or style; everything rendered from the server or the model uses `textContent`.
- Ownership without accounts: each browser receives an HttpOnly cookie, only its hash is stored on the server, and session listing, reading, changing, deleting, and spending are scoped to the owning browser. Past sessions for that browser sit behind one quiet link on the start page.
- Bilingual by use: the UI follows the browser language and can be switched on the page; the AI replies, the summary, and the picture follow the language spoken, and end phrases work in English and Chinese.
- Voice in: an AudioWorklet captures 24 kHz mono PCM in 80 ms frames over a WebSocket to the realtime endpoint of `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` (endpointing mode, cumulative partials). A push-to-talk fallback records WAV and transcribes it with the same model via file upload.
- Voice out: the browser's `speechSynthesis` with a voice in the language in use, for example a `zh-CN` voice for Chinese (there is no text-to-speech model). Interruptions are detected by comparing recognised text against what the AI just spoke. The final summary is spoken this way too, as soon as it is ready.
- The conductor: each turn sends the goal, current thinking state, and recent history to `muse-spark-1.3` with strict structured output. The model returns additions only, plus a single decision (listen / follow up / pull back / continue / answer / summarise / background task). Server rules ration speech (a minimum gap, silent `listen` turns) on top of the model's judgement.
- Background work (`muse-spark-1.3` with `web_search`, and drafting) runs on a thread pool, never blocks a turn, and announces one spoken sentence on completion. Paper sketches are understood by `muse-spark-1.3` from a photo; only what is visible on the paper is recorded.
- The final pass (`muse-spark-1.3`) reads every utterance at the end of a session and returns the cited summary, clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions described above; the server validates the citations and applies the later-statement-replaces-earlier rule before anything is shown.
- The picture (`muse-image-1.0`) is generated from the checked summary with web search turned off, at $0.01 per picture, and can be downloaded or redrawn from the result page.
- Ending is immediate at the page level: the result page lights up as soon as the session ends, and the summary, clean map, lists, and picture each fill in when ready. Sessions are one JSON file each, saved atomically after every turn, on the user's own machine.
- A phone launcher (`python -m app.phone`) serves the app over LAN HTTPS with a self-signed certificate and a random access token, because phones require HTTPS for the microphone. Data — sessions, the spend ledger, and the phone TLS files — is stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Blackout` on Windows and `~/.blackout` elsewhere; the spend ledger lives there regardless of `BLACKOUT_DATA_DIR`, with `BLACKOUT_LEDGER_FILE` as an explicit override. Spend is hard-capped locally by that ledger; the API key never reaches the browser or the logs, and speech and transcripts are never logged.
- Built for your own computer or LAN: a public deployment would also need per-visitor spending limits, an access code, and data expiry, which are not built yet.

## How it uses Meta models

- `muse-voice-transcribe-1.0` — speech recognition, in two modes that share one model: the realtime WebSocket endpoint (`wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime`) in endpointing mode with cumulative partials for hands-free listening, and file transcription of uploaded WAV for push-to-talk and goal dictation.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — conducting each turn: strict structured additions plus the listen / follow-up / pull-back / continue / answer / summarise decision, and whether to start background work.
- `muse-spark-1.3` with the built-in `web_search` tool — background search. Only the last message item is used; its first sentence is a short spoken conclusion, the rest and the sources are stored for the result page.
- `muse-spark-1.3` — background drafting, and sketch understanding from a photo of paper (only what is visible is recorded).
- `muse-spark-1.3` — the final pass: reading every utterance at the end of a session to produce the short summary, clean mind map, complete decisions and todos, and unresolved questions, each item citing the sentences it came from. The server drops any item without a valid citation, and treats a later statement as replacing an earlier one so a change of mind is not reported as a contradiction.
- `muse-image-1.0` — the one-page hand-drawn summary picture: timelines, flows, and lists with the exact text from the checked summary, generated with web search turned off, at $0.01 per picture, downloadable and redrawable from the result page. The explanation picture on the start page was drawn by Muse Image.
- Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`) and Muse Spark (`muse-spark-1.3`) — the coding models that generated this repository's code through the Meta Model API. Of the two, only `muse-spark-1.3` is also used by the running product; `muse-wonder-1.0` is not.

## Indie scope

Muse Spark and Muse Wonder, through the Meta Model API, generated all code in this repository, including the app, infrastructure, tests, and docs. The author provided the idea and tried the product. Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent) drafted the prompts in `spec/` from the author's idea, ran the generation, reviewed and tested the output, and made the git commits; a separate security review by Claude Code produced findings that Muse then fixed. Defects from review and use were written up in `spec/feedback_*.md`, the staged v2 build-out in `spec/stage_*.md`, and every fix was generated by Muse, including the infrastructure files, which were regenerated from `spec/feedback_05.md` without seeing the earlier source. Generation was run stage by stage rather than as one whole-project prompt, because a whole-project prompt made the model unreliable; `build_with_muse.py` was invoked with `--context` to supply the relevant files for each stage and `--expect` to declare the files that stage had to return. The first two commits contain earlier infrastructure files written by Claude Code.

No usage metrics or user anecdotes are claimed: Blackout has been tried by its author, and the limitations in the README (including what has and has not been exercised on real hardware) are stated there plainly.
